claims.text: The baseline material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy alloy in thin-film or nanoribbon form.
The baseline FeMnNiGeSi films are produced by sputter deposition.
The as-deposited films contain microstructural features and defects inherent to sputter deposition.
A conformal 10 nm diamond-like carbon overlayer can be deposited by ALD on the alloy films.
The proposed DLC overlayer has high thermal conductivity.
The proposed DLC overlayer is chemically inert toward the FeMnNiGeSi active layer.
Adding the DLC overlayer enhances thermal coupling at the film-overlayer interface and improves cross-plane heat dissipation.
Improved cross-plane heat dissipation accelerates heat transfer from the magnetocaloric layer to the environment.
Accelerated heat transfer reduces thermal lag during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Reduced thermal lag allows the magnetostructural transition to occur more rapidly and symmetrically.
Reduced thermal lag lowers magnetic hysteresis during magnetic-cooling cycles.
The DLC overlayer makes the magnetostructural transition more reversible despite the film's constrained dimensionality.
Relative to uncoated films, DLC-coated films will exhibit reduced hysteresis under fast cycling.
Relative to uncoated films, DLC-coated films will exhibit a sharper magnetic phase transition under fast cycling.
There will be a cycle-frequency threshold beyond which the overlayer produces no further improvement.
The proposed effect applies near the magnetic transition at applied fields of 5–50 mT and at low-to-moderate cycle frequencies.
The intervention is effective only if interfacial integrity is maintained without interdiffusion or stress-induced modification of the active layer.
The magnitude of hysteresis reduction and changes in magnetocaloric properties depend on overlayer deposition quality and interface characteristics.
